ps: But if you know me well enough, Eyiwetemi. I'm a quirky writer, reader, lover and hater, living in a city where it rains every other day. I also like lip gloss.

ps.t: It's funny in retrospect, but my literary journey started off because I was both a yapper and a liar. Yup. I started off lying for no apparent reason in primary school and  would make up stories and say they were from a movie only I have seen. And they believed me. Kids.

I was still doing that in my junior secondary. But in JSS 1, I wrote songs with my friends that kinda rhymed, and extended essays for English Language class. JSS 2 was my introduction to reading novels. I discovered romance on a spectrum from Harlequin to Christian authors like Karen Kingsbury, Francine Rivers and Jennifer Erin Valent. Secondary school me was finishing a 350-page novel in a day and a half because I had 3 other girls waiting to borrow it too. By senior school, I was writing my own silly romance stories in exercise books and passing them round to my friends.

Due to uni workload, I stopped writing stories and ventured into poetry as a way to express how I felt — usually about a boy. Now I write anything. It usually starts with a character with a particular trait, and then I build a whole world around them.
I'm a Warri babe that loves good food and soft life. I speak English and French, hold fast to my Christian faith, and I'm a romantic anti-romantic.

I can't dance, but I'm almost always listening to music. My favourite artistes are Lana Del Rey and Tanarelle. New places thrill me; the travelling it takes to reach them does not. I like when it rains and sweater weather.

Suya is my weakness. So is chocolate cake, ice cream, buttered or caramel popcorn, hot bread, barbecue... I could pretty much sell my soul for a good burger or sandwich. I love sweet and savoury meals and creamy coffee.

I build software for a living, and I love and hate my job equally. Outside of work, I read fiction and poems, write —or at least try to — and spend hours laughing at memes on X and/or getting ragebaited (the latter more than the former). When I really want to relax, I watch people play horror video games or make cozy Minecraft builds on YouTube, or an Asian drama that either has me swooning or pulling the hair from my head — oftentimes both.
On match days, I pray, hyperventilate, doubt then shout "Hala Madrid!". Proud Madrista.

secs.html:
Eyiwetemi is run by me, Georgina Awani, from Port Harcourt, Nigeria. I’m responsible for anything you share here, under the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023.

Write to privacy@eyiwetemi.com about anything on this page.

You can read everything here without an account, and I don’t ask who you are.

I count visits so I know what’s being read. I count views, finished chapters, which site sent you here, your country, and whether you’re on a phone or a computer. I don’t use cookies for this, I never store who you are, and nothing leaves this site.

When you make an account I keep your name, username and email, and your password in an encrypted form I can’t read. If you sign in with Google, Google sends me your name, email and photo instead.

Your name shows beside your comments. Likes and follows are counted, but only you can see which ones are yours.
If I invite you to review unpublished work, I use your email to send the invitation. You see only what I share with you, and your notes on it stay between us.

New work by email is sent from this site, not through a mailing company. I keep your email and the kinds of work you picked. Every email has a link to stop them, and stopping removes your address.

Notification emails follow your settings, and you can turn them off there.
One cookie keeps you signed in. Your theme is remembered in your own browser. Nothing here follows you to other sites.
I don’t sell what you give me or share it with anyone. The services that keep the site running hold it for me, and only so they can do that.
Delete your account in Settings and it goes at once, with your likes and follows. Your comments are deleted too. If someone replied to one, their reply stays, under “Comment deleted”.

You can ask to see what I hold about you, to correct it, or to have it deleted. Write to privacy@eyiwetemi.com. If you’re unhappy with my answer, you can complain to the Nigeria Data Protection Commission.
If this page changes in a way that matters, I’ll say so in a note.
